newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bond prices ended lower Tuesday in what one trader described as normal consolidation.

Swiss bond yields rose in contrast to German Bunds, where yields fell on perceptions that Bonn and the Bundesbank appeared to close to ending a rift over gold. The German government appeared ready to give up on a plan to revalue gold reserves to fill budget coffers, which would have helped it qualify for membership in the single European currency.
The spread between Swiss and German 10-year federal bond yields, which had widened to historic levels over 250 basis points, was back at around 240 basis points late on Tuesday.
Swiss federal bond prices may also have been pressured as investors sold Confederate bonds to offset purchases of a new one billion Swiss franc bond set by the government of Italy.
Italy's seven-year offering, priced at 102.25 at issue with a 3-1/4 percent coupon, yielded 3.25 to 3.27 percent on various screens late Tuesday.

The short end fell, with prices of three-month EuroSwiss futures traded on LIFFE down seven basis points. Speculation at some banks that a Swiss discount rate cut was in the offing may have been dampened by the Swiss franc's weaker tone on Tuesday, also versus the mark.
Euro Swiss francs down seven at 98.74.
